Package org.forgerock.openam.shared.security.whitelist

Class FailSafeRedirectUrlValidator<T>

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.forgerock.openam.shared.security.whitelist.FailSafeRedirectUrlValidator<T>
  • Type Parameters:
    T - The type identifying the configuration the whitelist is read from.
    public class FailSafeRedirectUrlValidator<T>
extends Object
    Validates redirect URLs that arrive as request parameters on endpoints which have no whitelist of their own.

    RedirectUrlValidator considers every URL valid when the configuration holds no patterns to match against, which makes it fail open on a default installation. This validator falls back to the origin of this server instead of allowing everything:

    • relative URLs are always accepted, they can not leave this server;
    • only http and https URLs are considered at all;
    • a URL pointing at this deployment - the same scheme, host and port as one of the origins this server answers on, and a path inside the context this server is deployed under - is accepted whether or not a whitelist exists, since it can not be an open redirect;
    • any other URL has to match the configured patterns, and is refused when there are none - unless a subclass asks for the legacy reading of an unconfigured whitelist through allowAnyUrlWithoutWhitelist();
    • when a whitelist could not be read at all, only the URLs of this deployment are accepted, whatever a subclass makes of an unconfigured one.

    This server answers on more than one origin, and each of them is accepted, because none is right on its own:

    • the com.iplanet.am.server.protocol, com.iplanet.am.server.host and com.iplanet.am.server.port properties, the same values the federation code builds its own local URL from. They are the only correct answer behind a TLS terminating proxy, where the servlet container sees the internal connection while the deployment is configured with the address browsers reach it at;
    • the origin the servlet container reports. It is the only correct answer on a site installation, where the properties above describe this instance rather than the load balancer in front of the site, and it is what OpenAM itself builds the URLs it hands out from - RPSigninRequest mints its wreply from HttpServletRequest.getRequestURL() and the SAML2 IdP proxy builds its RelayState from the Host header;
    • whatever a subclass adds through getAdditionalOrigins(HttpServletRequest, Collection) - the realm's Base URL Source service, for instance.

    The container view is derived from the Host header, so accepting it widens what counts as this server to whatever name resolves to it. That is the deployment's FQDN map to control, the same way it controls every other URL OpenAM builds from the header; a redirect lure cannot exploit it, because the header on the victim's request is the one their own browser sends.

    Host names are compared as they stand, apart from ASCII case, a trailing root label and the brackets of an IPv6 literal: a deployment whose name is an internationalised one has to name itself in com.iplanet.am.server.host in ASCII compatible form, the same the whitelist path expects of it.

      • isRedirectUrlValid

        public boolean isRedirectUrlValid​(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request,
                                  String url,
                                  Collection<T> configInfos)
        Tells whether it is safe to redirect to the given URL, considering several configurations.

        The whitelists of all the provided configurations are honoured together. This suits endpoints that can be reached for more than one role, where the caller can not tell up front which one holds the configuration.

        Parameters:
        request - The request being processed, consulted as one of the views of this server's origin, may be null.
        url - The URL to validate.
        configInfos - Identifies the configurations holding the whitelist, may be empty.
        Returns:
        true if the URL may be used in a redirect.

      • isOwnOriginRedirectUrl

        public boolean isOwnOriginRedirectUrl​(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request,
                                      String url)
        Tells whether it is safe to redirect to the given URL when the whitelist that governs it could not be consulted at all, because the caller could not work out which configuration holds it.

        An unreadable whitelist is not an empty one: allowAnyUrlWithoutWhitelist() has no say here, and the URL is only accepted when it is relative or points back at this deployment.

        Parameters:
        request - The request being processed, consulted as one of the views of this server's origin, may be null.
        url - The URL to validate.
        Returns:
        true if the URL may be used in a redirect.

      • allowAnyUrlWithoutWhitelist

        protected boolean allowAnyUrlWithoutWhitelist()
        Tells whether an unconfigured whitelist should be read the way RedirectUrlValidator reads it, as permission to redirect anywhere.

        Always false here: a subclass whose endpoints need an escape hatch for deployments that cannot populate the whitelist wires one in by overriding this. It has no say once the whitelist is populated, which is checked before this is reached, nor when the whitelist could not be read at all - an unreadable list is not an empty one, and reading it as one would hand the escape hatch to a deployment that did populate it.

        Returns:
        true to accept any http or https URL when no whitelist is configured.

      • getAdditionalOrigins

        protected Collection<String> getAdditionalOrigins​(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request,
                                                  Collection<T> configInfos)
        The origins this server answers on besides the one the container reports for the incoming request and the one it is configured with.

        This implementation adds none. It is only consulted once the other origins have already failed to match, so it costs nothing on the common path. Subclasses that can reach further configuration - the realm's Base URL Source service, for instance - override this and add to it.

        Parameters:
        request - The request being processed, may be null.
        configInfos - Identifies the configurations the origins may be read from, may be empty.
        Returns:
        The additional origins, never null and safe for a subclass to add to. Use addOrigin(Collection, String) so that what is added is normalised the same way.

      • getBareAuthority

        public static String getBareAuthority​(URI uri)
        Reads the authority of a URL whose host java.net.URI did not parse, where it is a bare host.

        The raw authority is read, not the decoded one: getAuthority() percent decodes, so https://v%C4%B1ct%C4%B1m.com/ would read as a host spelt with the dotless i, U+0131, which a browser resolves to xn--vctm-lzac.com and which a case insensitive comparison still takes for victim.com. Anything but an ASCII host and an optional numeric port is refused, which also refuses userinfo: getUserInfo() is null too when the authority did not parse, so the userinfo of openam@attacker.example.com would otherwise read as the host.

        Parameters:
        uri - The URL, whose getHost() is null.
        Returns:
        The authority as host or host:port, or null when the URL names none or names one that is not a bare host.
